title: Lay-Up Footwork Steps
description: Young players learn the right-hand and left-hand lay-up step by step: one step, then two steps, then a dribble into the two-step approach.

content.objective: Learn the opposite-foot take-off for each lay-up: right hand off the left foot, left hand off the right foot.
content.setup: A line at the right block (45 degrees, close) with a ball each; later at the free-throw line extended.
content.organization: One player at a time; rebound and rejoin.
instructions: Stage 1: stand one step away, step with the left foot and lift the right knee, lay the ball up with the right hand.
Stage 2: start two steps away: right foot, left foot, jump off the left and finish right.
Stage 3: one dribble, then the right-left steps and finish.
Aim for the top corner of the square.
Repeat all stages on the left side with the left hand.
coachingPoints: Opposite foot and hand: lift the knee on the shooting side.
commonMistakes: Jumping off the same foot as the shooting hand.
Throwing the ball at the rim instead of laying it up.
content.safety: Finishers land on two feet and clear the lane; the next player waits until the landing area is empty.
progressions: Start from the free-throw line extended with two dribbles.
regressions: Walk the steps without a ball first.
variations: Say the steps out loud ('right, left, up').
Lay-ups from a pass instead of a dribble.
successCriteria: Correct foot and hand on 8 of 10 lay-ups on each side.
content.gameApplication: The lay-up is the highest-percentage shot; correct footwork makes it reliable on both sides.
